_doc: Time-gated work that must NOT sit in queue.md as a parked item.
Emma, 2026-08-20: 'it waits until September 1, and waiting means you write a script that
injects it by a json into the queue or open questions at a certain date and the date is
Sept 21, so write that thing, because it being visible in the queue as "parked" adds
clutter, and other time gated stuff also goes into this, github actions injects on that
day into open questions and the queue.'
She named two dates in one sentence -- September 1, then 'the date is Sept 21'. The later,
more specific clause is taken as the spec; the first is recorded on the item itself so it
is not silently dropped. 09-21 also sits just after the Wikidata lockout lifts on 09-18,
which is where the other time-gated work clusters.
HOW IT WORKS: inject_due_items.py runs daily from GitHub Actions. On or after an item's
'due' date it appends the item to each of its targets and stamps 'injected'. Idempotent --
an HTML comment marker in the target is the real guard, so a reverted json cannot cause a
TO ADD ONE: append an object. 'due' is an ISO date, 'targets' is any of queue /
open-questions. Leave 'injected' null. Do not hand-edit 'injected' to re-fire an item --
remove the marker from the target instead, since the marker is the thing that decides.

items.title: continue-on-error on the five label-generator pipeline steps
body_md: ## Scheduled — `continue-on-error` on the label-generator pipelines
Deferred by Emma on 2026-08-20 to this date, and deliberately kept out of the queue in the
meantime: *"it being visible in the queue as 'parked' adds clutter."*
**The finding it came from (2026-08-20).** `label-generator-regenerate.yml` reported
**success** for two days while all five of its pipeline steps died on their first line
(`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'shinto_miraheze'`, a sys.path ordering bug, since
fixed). `continue-on-error: true` on every step is what bought that failure two days of
silence. The only visible traces were job time falling **12m24s to ~55s** and the commit
diff shrinking to a one-line date stamp — which reads as *"nothing needed regenerating"*.
**The decision, unchanged and still hers:** drop `continue-on-error` on the five steps so a
breakage goes red the same day; keep it so one bad pipeline cannot block the other four and
the docs step; or keep it and add a final step that fails the run if any pipeline exited
non-zero, which preserves the isolation and restores the signal.
This repo is **public**, so Actions minutes are free and a red run costs only the
notification. The repo already applies the strict version of this reasoning elsewhere:
`strip_husk_lines.py` is *"deliberately not continue-on-error: if the step cannot run, the
lines stay staged and the test stays red, which is the visible failure."*
body_wiki: * '''continue-on-error on the label-generator pipelines''' — deferred by you on 2026-08-20 to today, and kept out of queue.md in the meantime so it did not sit there as clutter.

** '''Your call:''' drop it (breakage goes red the same day) / keep it (one bad pipeline cannot block the rest) / keep it plus a final step that fails the run if any pipeline exited non-zero (keeps both).

than being treated as small enough to be an exception. That date has passed.

file is the authority, not this text.

necessarily two lines, because QuickStatements has no verb for overwriting a qualifier.
**Regenerate before pasting** rather than trusting any block written earlier — the generator
reads live state first, so an already-correct item emits nothing instead of a churn pair.
- **BLOCKED-ON-USER-ACTION** once the date passes: her account, her paste, no date on it and
nobody chasing it.

items.title: The 14 true duplicate part-of statements plus 10 confirmed leftovers
body_md: ## Scheduled — the 24 `part of` removals are unblocked
Held by the Wikidata lockout to **2026-09-18**. Re-read
`shinto_miraheze/wikidata_editing_lockout.state` before acting; the file decides, not this
text.
**14 true duplicates** (the same ordinal repeated) plus **10 confirmed leftovers** (the
blank-ordinal side, in the cases where the list itself names the item at the ordinal already
carried). Per-item evidence is committed at
`modern-quickstatements/p361_multi_part_of_audit.json`.
**This is the sequential-misc mechanism's job, not QuickStatements'** — which of two
*identical* statements gets removed is not expressible by value. The mechanism is built,
tested, and ships empty.
⚠️ **Do not widen this to the other classes.** The audit's other two are explicitly not
defects: **47** carry distinct ordinals and are legitimate, and **42** name the item nowhere
on the list side — those were folded into the orphan work by Emma on 2026-08-19, not into
this removal. A blanket strip would have been wrong for 45 of 55.
